x.around: Most hotels will have a selection of green tourist taxis, which have fixed prices to the most popular destinations. Yellow taxis are cheaper and more fun; locals buy a seat in a taxi on a journey from junction to junction for a few dalasi, or pay for a "town trip" to their destination. Minibuses and trucks are colourful, but extremely uncomfortable.

hidden.d: Gives good views over Banjul city. The gate is 35 m tall and the centre of an open square. It houses a textile museum.

x.intro: Banjul is the capital of Gambia and its fourth largest city. The city is on an island, which has constrained its size - its population is only 31,000 (2013). Consequently much of the population now is based on the mainland between the airport and the city. The main tourist and business centres are around Bakau, Fajara, Kotu and Serrekunda.

must.d: Small museum with cultural and historic artifacts

next.d: The Gambia's largest urban center, offering vibrant street life, craft markets, and access to the bustling Senegambia nightlife and dining strip.
Take the cross-river passenger and vehicle ferry from Banjul's port across the mouth of the Gambia River to Barra, the starting point for road travel north into Senegal toward Dakar.
(Kunta Kinteh Island): Located upriver near Juffureh, this UNESCO World Heritage Site preserves colonial-era ruins central to the transatlantic slave trade.

x.safe: Banjul is generally considered a safe capital with relatively low levels of violent crime, but basic precautions should still be observed

hidden.d: A 1000-ha reserve of mangroves, palm groves and savannahs with baboons, monkeys, birds and monitor lizards. About 45 min from Banjul - a D1300 taxi ride, and the driver will wait for you.

x.intro: Brikama is a city in Western Gambia and with a population of over 57,000, one of the largest in the Gambia.

next.d: Senegal. From there you can continue to Bissau, Guinea-Bissau's capital. Take the 'sept place' first to Selety, Senegal. The price is 65 GD plus 25 GD for one piece of baggage.

hidden.d: Visit the lively fisherman's village with the brightly painted fishing boats (pirogues) and its fisheries plant.
Explore the seemingly endless pristine beach of Gunjur. Take the sandy road at the bus stop.
One of the most beautiful beaches in Gambia. Public transport leaves from Serekunda and Brikama regularly, and private taxis can also be hired for day trips.

must.d: From Kuntaur just southwest of Wassu (but probably other places too), you can get a boat trip a few kilometres up river to the Baboon Islands on the Gambia River to see, among other things, chimpanzees.
Spread out on both sides of the border between Gambia and Senegal the stone circles are thought to have been erected around the 8th century to mark grave sites.

x.intro: Juffureh is a small town in the Gambia on the North Bank of the Gambia River, most famous as the reputed origin of Alex Haley's ancestor Kunta Kinte, as described in Haley's novel Roots.

intro: The Gambia is a small, narrow country along the length of the Gambia River in West Africa, almost completely surrounded by Senegal. Besides beaches and wildlife, The Gambia is known for the town of Juffureh, made famous by Alex Haley's Roots. It is known as the Smiling Coast. Famed for its warm winter weather, the Gambia's inland landscape provides lush river scenery and spiritual cultures.

other.d: mixed patched of thick forest and swamp most noteworthy for its migratory birds but also home to dugongs, otters, hogs, antelope, & hippos.
one of the largest and most important wildlife reserves in the country.

x.safe: The park's tourist infrastructure is underdeveloped. You'll likely be venturing about on your own. Watch for snakes!

other.d: a remainder from the slave trade and a UNESCO World Heritage site

x.around: The island is small and, alas, getting even smaller, so you will get around on foot.
x.intro: Kunta Kinteh Island, formerly called James Island, is an island in the Gambia River, 30 km from the river mouth. The island and some nearby areas are on the UNESCO World Heritage List because they have important relics of the West African slave trade. In Alex Haley's book and TV series Roots, Kunta Kinteh is brought by slave ship from this island to Maryland in the US.

other.d: Beautiful national park below Janjanbureh. The camp is pricey, but worth the money. They will organize boat tours to see chimpanzees, baboons, monkeys, and crocodiles.
